scientific_question: For historical actions produced by a real older upstream Home Assistant controller revision, which actions remain semantically authorized after a real upstream controller update that retires redundant set_preset_mode calls?

source_semantics.action_rule: unconditionally invoke climate.set_preset_mode(target_preset) whenever the enabled automation runs
invoke climate.set_preset_mode(target_preset) only when current preset_mode differs from target_preset; optional writeback branch exists but is disabled in VE1

source_change_claim.result_bearing_change: old always emits set_preset_mode; new suppresses the call when current_preset equals target_preset
source_change_claim.update_motivation_from_upstream_source: avoid resetting manual target temperature every minute when the requested preset is already active

evaluated_profile.profile_name: frozen four-preset Better Thermostat evaluation profile
evaluated_profile.scope_guardrail: VE1 does not claim to cover the blueprint's full optional boost/eco/activity/writeback configuration space.

claim_projection.compatibility_definition: old historical projected action is compatible iff it equals the new target projected action for the same evaluated state

pre_result_expected_split.derivation: For each of the 8 presence×motion×night combinations the target preset is unique. Across the 4 current_preset values, exactly 1 equals that target and 3 differ. Old always emits SET(target); new emits NO_ACTION only in the equal case.

policies.replay_all: execute the old historical action in every state
policies.version_lock: because the upstream revision differs, discard all old history and invoke the new native controller in every state
policies.replaymark: reuse only old historical actions semantically authorized by the new target; BLOCK_REUSE leaves native recovery to the caller
policies.direct_reference: fresh unchanged new upstream controller execution

pre_result_policy_predictions.note: These are protocol predictions implied by the pinned source semantics and evaluated finite profile, not observed results.

future_measurement_boundary.causal_rule: pre-action state must be fixed before controller invocation; post-action global state may never be used as the decision-state measurement
future_measurement_boundary.reason: SA1 demonstrated that post-trigger global state can reflect post-action mutation. VE1 therefore freezes a pre-action boundary prospectively and does not inherit SA1's failed measurement rule.
raw_authority: exact native service event or verified absence

nonclaims: VE1 does not infer arbitrary Home Assistant/Jinja semantics.
VE1 does not establish semantic compatibility for the blueprint's optional boost/eco/activity/writeback modes.
VE1 does not claim version hashes are sufficient semantic compatibility criteria.
VE1 does not modify the already-sealed C3/C4/C5 evidence.
VE1 does not turn ReplayMark into a native fallback owner.
next_gate: Freeze a canonical 32-row expected cross-version compatibility table and a source-identity/static verifier before any live execution capsule is opened.
